text:
javier: FYI customer ACME reported sustained 429s on their Dedicated pool (qz-prod) starting ~2026-03-12 09:20 UTC. They have reserved capacity but we're returning throttles. Ticket #4521

maria: can you paste a sample request id + headers?

javier: sample curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME' \n  -H 'X-Redwood-Tier: [\"gold\"]' \n  -d '{"model":"rw-large","prompt":"hi"}'
```
response: HTTP 429, body: {"error":"rate_limited","pool":"shared-low-prio","quota_used":0.98}
request_id: r-0a1b2c

sam: that's suspicious — header is a JSON array string. We shipped a header-parsing relaxation last week; I think arrays are being treated as literal instead of normalized token. Policy eval then falls back to default pool (shared-low-prio).

ingrid: I pulled control-plane route logs for r-0a1b2c:
route_eval=[{"policy":"tier-match","input":"[\"gold\"]","match":false},{"policy":"default-fallback","match":true,"pool":"shared-low-prio"}]
looks like parser returned the raw string '[\"gold\"]' instead of normalized 'gold' so matcher missed.

maria: repro script for eng (staging):
```
for i in {1..5}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-TEST" -H "X-Redwood-Tier: [\"gold\"]" https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
done
```
You can repro routing to shared-low-prio.

support_lead: mitigation for customer? they need hot workaround.

sam: temporary mitigation applied — set control-plane env ROUTE_HEADER_STRICT=true to enforce tokenized header parsing. I pushed a hotfix and restarted control-plane pods in prod-us-west-2. deploy-bot: rollout control-plane v1.12.7-hotfix -> prod-us-west-2 :rocket:

deploy-bot: rolled out control-plane v1.12.7-hotfix to prod-us-west-2 at 2026-03-12T09:45:12Z (sha: d4c3f2).

javier: ACME confirmed errors dropped within 5m after the restart. They want root cause and a permanent fix.

ingrid: root cause: commit 0f9ab (v1.12.6) relaxed header parsing; it returns bracketed values as literal strings when client sends JSON-array style headers. The policy matcher expects normalized scalar tokens and doesn't unquote arrays. I'll open a PR to normalize header values during route evaluation + add unit tests.

support_lead: assigning eng-runtime + eng-sre. Owners: @ingrid, @sam. Please prepare regression alert, postmortem, and a changelog entry.

javier: I'll update the customer with the workaround (send X-Redwood-Tier: gold) and ETA for the patch. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
